**Subject:** Refund of Rs 18,499 for a returned mobile phone – your rights and the steps you can take in Jaipur --- ### 1. Governing Law | Law | Key Provisions Relevant to Your Case | |-----|--------------------------------------| | **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA‑2019)** | • **Section 2(1)(g)** – “consumer” includes a buyer of goods through an online marketplace.
• **Section 2(1)(r)** – “deficiency” includes failure to provide a refund within a reasonable time.
• **Section 19** – Consumer can file a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF) for claims up to ₹1 crore. | | **The Sale of Goods Act, 1930** (as applied to e‑commerce) | • **Section 16** – When the buyer returns goods, the seller must return the price (or part thereof) within a reasonable time. | | **Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021** | • Intermediaries (e‑commerce platforms) must provide a **“grievance redressal mechanism”** and **“timely resolution”** of consumer complaints. | | **E‑Commerce Rules, 2020 (under the Consumer Protection (E‑Commerce) Rules, 2020)** | • **Rule 9** – Sellers must **refund the purchase price within 7 days** of receiving the returned product, failing which a penalty may be imposed. | --- ### 2. What the law says about refunds for returned goods 1. **Refund time‑frame** – Under the E‑Commerce Rules, 2020 (Rule 9), the seller must **refund the amount within 7 days** of receipt of the returned product. 2. **Reasonable time** – The CPA‑2019 treats any delay beyond the statutory period as a “deficiency” (Sec. 2(1)(r)). 3. **Penalty for non‑compliance** – The platform can be penalised up to **₹10 lakhs** per violation (Rule 9(2)). 4. **Consumer’s remedy** – You may: * **Send a legal notice** (demand letter) to the seller/marketplace. * **File a complaint** before the **Jaipur District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** (jurisdiction up to ₹1 crore). * Claim **interest** on the delayed amount (generally 12% per annum under Sec. 73 of the CPA‑2019) and **compensation for mental agony** (usually nominal, e.g., ₹5,000‑₹10,000). --- ### 3. Practical steps you should take **right now** | Step | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Gather documentary evidence** | • Order confirmation (email/SMS) showing Rs 18,499 price.
• Pickup receipt / courier tracking showing the product was collected on **10 Sept 2026**.
• All four ticket numbers, dates, and screenshots of the “under process” status.
• Any email/WhatsApp communication with the seller or platform. | Evidence is essential for a consumer forum and for a legal notice. | | **2. Send a **formal legal notice** (demand letter)** | • Draft a notice on a **lawyer’s letterhead** demanding **full refund + 12% p.a. interest** for the period from 10 Sept 2026 to the date of payment, and **₹10,000 compensation** for inconvenience.
• Mention the statutory provisions (E‑Commerce Rules 9, CPA‑2019 Sec. 19, Sec. 73).
• Set a **strict deadline of 7 days** from receipt of the notice. | A demand notice often forces the seller/platform to settle to avoid litigation. | | **3. File a complaint with the **Jaipur District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** (DCDRF)** | • Use **Form‑1** (available on the Rajasthan State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission website).
• Attach all evidence and a copy of the legal notice (if you have sent it).
• Pay the prescribed court fee (₹100 for claims up to ₹10,000; ₹500 for claims up to ₹1 lac).
• You can file **online** through the **e‑Courts portal** (https://ecourts.gov.in). | The DCDRF can pass an order directing the seller to refund the amount, interest, and compensation, and may also impose a penalty on the e‑commerce platform. | | **4. Escalate on the platform’s grievance portal** | • Use the **“Escalation”** or “**Contact Senior Management**” option.
• Mention the **Consumer Protection (E‑Commerce) Rules, 2020** and that you have already filed a legal notice. | Some platforms act quickly when they see a formal legal step is underway. | | **5. Notify the **Rajasthan State Consumer Helpline (1800‑11‑4000)** | • Register a complaint; the helpline can mediate and may pressure the platform to act. | Helpline intervention can sometimes bring a quicker settlement. | --- ### 4. Sample wording for the **legal notice** (you can give this to a lawyer) ``` [Your Name] [Your Address] Jaipur, Rajasthan – 302001 Date: ___ To, [Seller/Marketplace Name] [Address of Seller/Marketplace] Subject: Legal Notice for Immediate Refund of Rs. 18,499 (Order ID: OD12345) with Interest and Compensation Dear Sir/Madam, 1. I, [Your Name], purchased a mobile phone (Order ID: OD12345) on your platform on [date of purchase] for Rs. 18,499. The product was returned on 10 September 2026, and the courier pickup was confirmed (copy attached). 2. Under the **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** (Sec. 2(1)(r) – deficiency) and **E‑Commerce Rules, 2020** (Rule 9), you are statutorily required to refund the purchase price within **7 days** of receipt of the returned goods. Despite four tickets raised (latest on 1 Oct 2026) you have failed to do so. 3. Consequently, you are in breach of the above statutes and liable to: a) Refund the full amount of Rs. 18,499; b) Pay interest at 12% per annum from 10 Sept 2026 to the date of actual payment; c) Pay compensation of Rs. 10,000 for mental agony and inconvenience; d) Bear the cost of this notice. 4. You are hereby **required to make the payment within 7 days** from receipt of this notice. Failure to comply will compel me to file a complaint before the **Jaipur District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** and seek appropriate relief, including a penalty under the E‑Commerce Rules. Please treat this notice as a final opportunity to settle the matter amicably. Yours faithfully, [Signature] [Your Name] [Contact No. / Email] ``` --- ### 5. Timeline you can realistically expect | Action | Approx. Time | |--------|--------------| | Send legal notice (by registered post/e‑mail) | Day 0 | | Seller’s response (if any) | ≤ 7 days | | If no response → File DCDRF complaint | Within 15 days of notice | | DCDRF hearing (first date) | Usually within 30‑45 days of filing | | Final order (including interest & compensation) | Typically 3‑6 months from filing, but interim orders for refund can be passed earlier. | --- ### 6. Important points to remember 1. **Keep all communications** in electronic form (screenshots, PDFs). 2. **Do not accept a “partial” refund** or a “store credit” unless you expressly agree in writing. 3. **Interest calculation**: 12% p.a. on Rs 18,499 for, say, 60 days (from 10 Sept to 9 Nov) = \[ \frac{12}{100} \times \frac{60}{365} \times 18,499 \approx Rs.\, 365 \] Include this in your demand. 4. If the platform is an **intermediary** (e.g., Amazon, Flipkart), you can also invoke **Section 79 of the IT Act, 2000** to compel them to act, but the consumer forum will treat the platform as a “seller” for the purpose of the CPA‑2019. --- ### 7. Bottom line - **Statutory right:** Refund within **7 days** of return (E‑Commerce Rules, 2020). - **Your remedy:** Send a legal notice, then file a complaint before the **Jaipur District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** for the amount, interest, and compensation. - **Potential outcome:** The forum can order the seller/platform to pay **Rs 18,499 + interest + compensation**, and may also impose a penalty on the platform for non‑compliance. If you need a lawyer to draft the notice or to represent you before the consumer forum, let me know and I can suggest a few reputable consumer‑law practitioners in Jaipur. --- **Stay firm and keep a clear paper‑trail; the law is on your side.**
